restarting: The server is restarting… The game will carry on by itself.
resumeFill: Fill in from a previous game
resumeFilled: Filled in from the game on {date}. You can change anything.
resumeHint: If a previous game was cut short, the game starts from the chosen round with these points.
resumeNone: No previous games of this quiz found.
resumeUnmatched: Not found in that game, stays at 0: {names}
retryChoice: Partly correct: {points}. Keep it or try again?
revealBluffTop_one: Most votes: the fib by {names} — {count} vote
revealBluffTop_other: Most votes: the fib by {names} — {count} votes
revealHint: The picture is emerging: the sooner you answer, the more points you get.
revealNow: Now: up to {percent}% of the value
riskMine: ⚄ Risk: correct — ×3, a mistake or silence — minus the full value
roundBriefPreview: This is how players will see the round on the intro
roundDescriptionPlaceholder: Optional. For example, all questions about films from the 90s
roundHow_auction: Before each question there is bidding: only the theme and the price are visible. Whoever bids the most answers: correct — the price and the bid, wrong — minus. No bids — everyone answers.
roundHow_bets: Before every question — a secret bet: only the start of the question is visible. The minimum bet grows with each question. A wrong answer gives the bet to the bank, correct ones share it.
roundHow_blitz: Know the answer? Press “Answer” on your phone to join the queue.
roundHow_blitzInstant: There's no button: answer on your phone straight away — speed matters.
roundHow_board: First the order: everyone rolls a die on their phone (or the host sets the order). On your turn, pick a cell — a category and a value.
roundHow_boardAuto: First the order: everyone rolls a die on their phone. On your turn, pick a cell — a category and a value.
roundHow_classic: Questions come one by one; everyone answers on their own phone.
roundHow_final: First a secret stake on your phone, then one question for everyone.
roundHow_ladder: One contestant climbs a ladder of questions and can take the winnings at any moment. Everyone else answers for themselves — a correct answer earns 10% of the level's amount.
roundHow_puzzles: Everyone solves a sudoku or a crossword, builds a jigsaw, spots the differences or matches pairs of cards on their phone; in teams it is one shared puzzle that anyone can work on. “Done” locks in a grid, and whether it is right shows only after time is up.
roundHow_quest: Answer the questions — every correct one opens a symbol of the code. Know the answer to the main question? Enter the code at any time: the earlier, the bigger the bonus.
roundHow_survival: Whoever gets it wrong or stays silent goes “on the edge” and faces a trial. Whoever fails it becomes a ghost and plays just for themselves.
roundHow_truth: Everyone writes a little-known fact about themselves in the lobby. In the round the fact is on screen and you pick who wrote it. A correct guess earns the question price; the author earns points for everyone who guessed wrong.
roundHow_wipeout: A correct answer adds the value to the bank, a mistake burns it. After each correct one — “Next” or “Take”.
ruleMinus: Penalty: minus the question's value for a wrong answer
ruleSeriesMinus: Minus streak: each wrong answer in a row takes one step more
ruleSeriesMinusPenalty: The minus streak already penalizes mistakes
ruleSeriesPlus: Plus streak: each correct answer in a row gives one step more
ruleStreak: Streaks: a bonus for correct answers in a row
sameTimeTitle: Same time for all questions in the round
saveConfirm: Save the game and close the room? An unfinished question will start over. You'll continue from “Game history”.
savedRestartNote: Will resume from the start of the round (app update)
scopeZoom: The target is in the frame on the map
scoreSource_carry: Carried over from a previous game
shelfEmpty: The shelf is empty for now — your trophies will stand here.
shopBlock_bought: You've already bought a debuff until the next question
shopNote: Kicks in on the next question your rival answers.
shopWarded: has a charm: the first debuff will fizzle out
signInToKeep: Sign in to save the game in “My games”
sliderHint: Within the tolerance — full points; beyond it, points fall to zero at the “zero points” limit. With no limit — full points or nothing. Half the value or more counts as a correct answer.
sliderOnPhone: Drag the slider on your phone: from {min} to {max}
sliderZeroInvalid: Enter a number or leave the field empty.
slotReleaseConfirm: Free up the place of “{nickname}”? The points will stay in the table.
slotReleased: The host freed up your place. Pick yourself again.
sortCellNote: Only the player who picked the cell sorts, from their phone. Points for each sorted word.
sortHint: Players see the categories at the edges of the screen and sort the words one at a time. After a mistake the word goes to the end of the queue and the player's screen freezes for the set number of seconds.
sortHintPlayer: Drag the word into a category, tap the category or press an arrow.
sortNoWinner: No one managed to sort all the words
sortOnPhone: Sort the words on your phone
sortTotal_one: Up to {total} point in total (no more than 2000)
sortTotal_other: Up to {total} points in total (no more than 2000)
sparesHint: For the “Swap question” buff in classic rounds (and on the board, while no category has its own spares). Points and time come from the current question.
speedBonus: Speed points: a faster correct answer earns more
spellingHint: Add every variant that should count: name and nickname, full and short name, in Cyrillic and in Latin letters. Case, quotes, apostrophes and extra spaces are ignored. The host can accept an answer by hand, but the bot only uses this list.
spotdiffAspectBad: The picture is too wide or too tall: the aspect ratio must be between 1 : 2 and 3 : 1.
spotdiffAspectMismatch: The second picture must have the same aspect ratio as the first (within 2 %).
spotdiffDoneIn: All found in {time} s. Waiting for the others
spotdiffLowRes: The picture is only {width} px wide — it will look blurry on a big screen. Better from {min} px.
spotdiffMarkHint: Tap the second picture to put a circle on a difference; drag to change the radius. Tap a circle to select it.
spotdiffOffline: No connection — tap again when it is back.
spotlightVoice: The player is answering out loud
spotlightWaitNumber: The answer as a number will appear here
spotlightWaitText: The answer in words will appear here
studioBackdropHint: The backdrop shows on the stage and in the full view.
studioCalmNote: "Reduce motion" is on: effects stay still and the appearance does not play.
studioCropHint: Drag the photo to move the frame
studioEngraving: Caption under the trophy and on the certificate
studioMovedTo: “{from}” is taken ({what}), so it is here: “{to}”.
studioNoPlace: Does not fit: “{from}” is taken ({what}) and there is no free place.
studioNoWebgl: This device can't show 3D. The prize will be saved with all its decoration, and anyone whose device shows 3D will see the trophy.
studioNotFound: There's no such prize in your stock.
studioPlaqueTaken: A photo is already on the plaque.
studioPremiumHint: Premium: special shapes and materials. For now they unlock with your level.
studioReadOnly: The prize is set in a game — you can only view it.
studioRotateHint: Drag the trophy with your finger to turn it
studioStickerMax: There are already {n} stickers — no more allowed.
studioStickerNoRoom: No free places — remove something to add a sticker.
sudokuConflict: A repeat in a row, column or box — the cells are highlighted.
sudokuCustomHint: Digits 1–6; the arrow keys move between cells, Backspace clears.
sudokuGenerateConfirm: Generate a new grid? Your digits will be lost.
sudokuHelp: Players see only the given digits; the host console sees the solution, and everyone sees it after time is up.
sudokuMany: There are several solutions — add digits.
sudokuNone: There is no solution — check the digits.
summaryAuctionFree: A bid is any amount higher than the current one
summaryAuctionLossPrice: A mistake costs the bid and the question price
summaryBetsAll: You can bet all your points
summaryBetsMinimumFlat: Minimum bet: {start}, the same for the whole round
summaryBlitz: Only the first to answer correctly gets points.
summaryBlitzHow: Press “Answer” to join the queue, and answer {window}.
summaryBlitzInstant: Answer straight away, no button: one try, answers are checked in the order they arrive.
summaryBoard: Players take turns picking a cell; whoever picked it answers.
summaryBoardBlitz: On a blitz cell the first to answer correctly gets the points; if it's whoever picked the cell, the value is doubled.
summaryBoardMixed: The answer is given on the phone or out loud, depending on the cell.
summaryBoardPhone: The answer is given on the phone.
summaryBoardVoice: The answer is given out loud, the host judges it.
summaryClassic: Everyone answers: everyone who answers correctly gets points.
summaryFinal: Everyone secretly stakes from 0 up to their score.
summaryFinalBank: Whoever gets it wrong or doesn't answer gives their stake to the shared bank; whoever answers correctly keeps theirs and shares the bank in proportion to the stakes.
summaryFinalScore: A correct answer — plus the stake, a wrong one or none — minus the stake.
summaryLadderContestant: The contestant climbs the ladder up to {top}: a mistake leaves only the safe amount, “Take” gives the amount of the level reached.
summaryLadderHall: Everyone else answers for themselves: correct — 10% of the level's amount.
summaryLadderPick_lowest: Whoever has the fewest points goes.
summaryLadderPick_random: A draw will pick the contestant.
summaryMelodies_one: {count} tune: points by the longest snippet heard
summaryMelodies_other: {count} tunes: points by the longest snippet heard
summaryPenaltyAll: Some blitz cells: minus for everyone except whoever got it right
summaryPenaltyCells: Mistake on a normal cell: minus the question's value
summaryPuzzles: Points only for a fully correct grid; in a crossword with a key word, for the key word; a jigsaw is scored by speed
summaryQuestBuff: The bonus is one more “{buff}” buff
summaryQuestBuffFirst: The bonus is one more “{buff}” buff, only for the first {first}
summaryQuestPoints: A bonus of up to {points} points — the earlier, the more
summarySeriesMinus: streak: each wrong answer in a row −{step}
summarySeriesPlus: streak: each correct answer in a row +{step}
summarySpeed: If there's a timer, a faster correct answer earns more points.
summarySurvival: Points work as in a classic round. A mistake or silence puts you “on the edge” and you face a trial; fail it and you become a ghost with no points.
summarySurvivalBonus: Whoever survives to the end gets +{bonus}.
summarySurvivalTrial_luck: The trial is luck: one of three doors hides a trap.
summarySurvivalTrial_question: The trial is a separate survival question.
summaryTruth: Questions are players’ facts; a correct guess earns {points}, the author earns a share for each player who missed
summaryWipeout: Correct — the value goes into the bank; a mistake or silence — the bank goes up in smoke and you watch until the end of the round.
summaryWipeoutTake: After each correct answer, choose “Next” or “Take”: what you take goes into your points. After the last question the bank carries over by itself.
surveyBoardOnStage: The board is on the screen
surveyCellNote: "100 to 1" is only played by phone on a normal cell.
surveyCloudHint: The board is built during the game: up to 8 of the most frequent words, popularity is the share of players who wrote the word. Words you've hidden won't get in.
surveyFromCloud: A board from your answers in the word cloud
surveyHint: Name up to {n} of the most popular answers
surveyMultiple: The poll allowed more than one answer
surveyNoClouds: Add a “word cloud” earlier in a classic round — the board will be built from its answers.
surveyOnPhone: Write up to {n} answers on your phone
surveyPointsHint: A row with popularity 30 gives 30% of the value. A player can't get more than the value.
surveySkipHint: If the cloud doesn't give a single word, the question will be skipped.
surveySkipped: Question “{text}” skipped: the cloud gave no words and there are no spare rows.
surveySpare: Spare rows if the cloud is empty
surveySpareDropConfirm: Spare rows with text will disappear. Turn them off?
survivalAllWrong: Everyone got it wrong — no one is out.
survivalBonusGot: You made it to the end: +{bonus}
survivalDoorDefault: If you don't choose within {seconds} s, a door will be picked for you.
survivalEdge: You're on the edge — trial time.
survivalFellBack: No survival questions left — it's luck.
survivalGhostBanner: You're a ghost: answer for yourself — no points.
survivalOut: You're out — now you're a ghost.
survivalOutAfter: You were knocked out after question {n}.
survivalTrialsHint: One question per trial, in order. When they run out, it's luck.
survivalTrialsLuckNote: With luck these questions aren't needed.
tableOwnOnly: The full table comes at the end of the game.
teamCaptainDecides: The captain is deciding for the team…
teamCaptainWager: The captain stakes for the team
teamDiceTitle: Rolling the dice: the highest go into one team
teamDuelistPick: Who from the team goes to the duel?
teamStartFew: To start, you need people in at least two teams
teamStartHint: Without a team: {count} — we'll assign them at the start
teamWaitBot: The bot will split the teams as soon as the author starts the game.
teamWaitHost: The host is splitting the teams…
teamWatchAnswerer: {name} is answering — give advice out loud
teamWatchBuzzer: {name} is answering — give advice out loud
teamWatchLead: Captain {name} is answering — give advice out loud
teamsHint: The host picks the team line-ups in the lobby before each game.
timedlistCellNote: A timed list is played only by phone on a normal cell. The price is per item.
toleranceHint: 0 means only the exact answer. Otherwise, the closer to the number, the more points.
truthEditorNote: The game creates the questions itself when the round starts — one for each fact the players write in the lobby. With no facts, the round is skipped.
truthFactHidden: The host hid your fact — write another one.
truthFactHint: Something few people know about you. It will be shown in the «The Truth About a Player» round, and the others will guess whose it is.
truthFactWrite: Write a fact for the «The Truth About a Player» round
truthHostNone: Nobody has written a fact yet
truthOwn: This is your fact — the others do the guessing.
truthOwnTeam: This is your team's fact — the others do the guessing.
truthSkipped: No facts — the «The Truth About a Player» round is skipped.
typeHowCluesSelf: You reveal clues yourself with the “Another clue” button — each lowers the value. Answer as soon as you know; one try only.
typeHow_bluff: First make up a fake answer to fool the others, then find the truth among the fibs.
typeHow_chain: Guess the hidden words in turn, each linked to the previous one. A hint reveals a letter but adds seconds to your time.
typeHow_clues: Clues are revealed one at a time — answer as soon as you know. The sooner, the more points; one try only.
typeHow_crossword: Fill in the words from the clues: tap a cell to pick a word. When you finish, tap “Done”.
typeHow_drawing: One player draws a word on the phone, the others guess: type the word you see in the drawing.
typeHow_jigsaw: Put the picture together from pieces: drag a piece into place, tap it to turn it. The faster you finish, the more points.
typeHow_letterwords: Make as many words as you can from the set of letters, or one longest word. Only nouns in the nominative singular count.
typeHow_match: Make the pairs: tap an item on the left, then on the right, and press “Answer”.
typeHow_melody: Listen to a snippet of a tune and type its title. You open the snippets yourself: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds. The shorter the snippet you guess on, the more points: 100, 80, 60, 40 or 25 % of the price. You get one try.
typeHow_memory: Flip two cards at a time and look for pairs: a found pair stays open, and a wrong pair closes again after a second. Whoever finds all the pairs faster scores more; whoever does not find them all gets 0.
typeHow_moreless: A row of comparisons: in each, choose which of the two options is right.
typeHow_multi: Mark all the correct options and press “Answer”.
typeHow_order: Arrange the rows with the ↑ ↓ arrows and press “Answer”.
typeHow_orderTop: Arrange the rows with the ↑ ↓ arrows (top — {top}) and press “Answer”.
typeHow_pin: Tap the map to place a pin, pinch with two fingers to zoom in, and press “Answer”.
typeHow_poll: There's no correct answer — just pick your option. No points.
typeHow_slider: Drag the slider to your number and press “Answer”.
typeHow_sort: Sort the words into categories: drag the card or tap a category. After a mistake the screen freezes briefly.
typeHow_spotdiff: Two almost identical pictures: tap the spot where they differ. Each find earns a share of the points, all of them the full price. Three misses in a row freeze you for a second, and every further miss in a row makes the pause a second longer (up to 5).
typeHow_sudoku: Fill the 6×6 grid with digits 1–6: no repeats in any row, column or 2×3 box. When you finish, tap “Done”.
typeHow_survey: Guess the most popular answers to a poll: write up to a few options. The more popular the answer, the more points.
typeHow_timedlist: Name as many items from a hidden list as you can. The rarer the find, the more points.
typeHow_wall: Find groups of tiles with a common link: select the tiles of one group and press “Check”. Only a few mistakes are allowed.
typeHow_wordcloud: Write up to three short words. The more often a word comes up, the bigger it is on screen. No points.
typeHow_wordladder: Get from the start word to the target word, changing one letter at a time. Every word is a noun. Fewer steps, more points.
typeOnPhone: Type your answer on your phone
undoConfirmQuestion: Undo the points of {who} for question {question}?
undoConfirmRound: Undo the points of {who} for round {round}?
undoEmpty: Nothing to undo yet. A question's points will appear here as soon as the question closes.
undoNoticeMany: The host undid the points of {who} ({where})
videoInvalid: That's not a link to a YouTube video
videoTitleHidden: Video title hidden until the answer
voteAsk: {name} asks the room: what do you think?
wagerModeBankHint: Whoever gets it wrong gives their stake to the bank; whoever gets it right shares the bank in proportion to their stakes.
wagerModeClassicHint: A correct answer adds the stake, a wrong one takes it away.
wallCellNote: The wall is only solved by phone on a normal cell.
wallGroupNameHint: Players will only see the name at the reveal.
wallLocked: The wall is locked: no mistakes left. Groups found: {found}.
wallOnPhone: Find the groups on your phone
wallOrderHint: Write the groups in any order: players will see the tiles shuffled.
wallPointsHint: Each group is worth {per} points. The last one solves itself, so the whole wall is worth {max}.
wallShrinkConfirm: The last group and the last tiles will disappear. Continue?
wallSolved: Wall solved! The last group was put together for you.
wipeoutBurned: The bank went up in smoke
wipeoutDefault: If you don't choose within {seconds} s, the bank is taken automatically.
wipeoutMinHint: “All in” can't have fewer than {min} questions.
wipeoutOut: You're no longer playing this round — watch.
wipeoutSettingsNote: “All in” has no point rules, buffs, debuffs or duels.
wipeoutStayed: You're going on. Waiting for the others…
wordLadderHint: Set at least one correct path. Players change one letter at a time; every word is a noun in the nominative singular. Whoever gets there in the fewest steps gets the full price; past the maximum number of steps it's 0.
wordLadderOnPhone: Build the ladder on your phone
wordLadderOut: You didn't reach the target in time
wordLadderUnknown: Not in the dictionary: {words}. These words will still count in the game.
xpRules: XP comes from games with at least 3 players with accounts and 5 questions. Not for your own quiz or for replaying the same one. Up to 600 a day; achievements count on top of that.
